about.title: Nevada City Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Nevada City's mix of narrow, winding roads and busy corridors like SR-49 and State Route 20 means collisions happen even in a town this small. Recent records show 11 injury collisions and 14 people hurt in a single year here, with Monday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. showing up often in the reports — likely tied to commuters and end-of-day traffic squeezing through town. Whether you were driving, a passenger, or on foot near one of these corridors, the aftermath can mean medical bills, missed work, and confusing calls from insurance adjusters. We handle personal injury claims from Nevada City car crashes. Our team can evaluate your claim, deal with insurers, and explain your options under California law. There's no cost for an initial consultation, and we work on contingency, meaning no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls Back

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government road or vehicle was involved. We can help you figure out which deadline applies before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Your Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by the percentage of blame assigned to you — even if that share is small. We can review the crash details before you speak with the other driver's insurer to help protect your share of any recovery.

items.title: No Cap Doesn't Mean No Fight
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, but insurers still push back hard on these claims. Our team can help document your losses and advise you on how to avoid giving a recorded statement that could later be used against you.

items.question: I was in a crash on SR-49 near Nevada City — should I talk to the other driver's insurance company first?
items.answer: It's generally safer to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can shift blame or minimize your injuries. We can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Nevada County?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, like the county or state, was involved in causing the crash, that deadline can be as short as six months. It's worth getting a quick evaluation early so you don't miss a critical date.

items.question: What does it cost to speak with your team about my Nevada City car accident?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer free initial consultations, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront fee to speak with us about your Nevada City car accident.
